clue.text: Very cold parrot starting a course of action

indicators.note: only the starting part of the parrot's pet name is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot
very cold means icy

explanation.surface: A frozen parrot embarks on some plan of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' is a trimming: only the opening part of the parrot's name survives, not just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy is a chosen plan or principle of action adopted by a person or body.

clue.text: Nothing against a bit of work — to keep busy I left women for an overbooked gathering

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: the unit holds the rearranged letters inside itself, as if keeping them

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters are bustling about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the women to stay occupied, at an event with too many people booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is the anagram signal for I LEFT WOMEN, giving FLOWMEETIN; 'to keep' has the work unit hold it. 'a bit of work' is a physics unit, not a task.
explanation.definitionFit: An overflow meeting is an extra session for people who cannot fit into the main, oversubscribed one.

clue.text: Sarcastic talk brings club to untimely end

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

indicators.note: the end of the word untimely means its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone's sneering remarks lead to a golf club meeting a premature finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is speech that says the opposite of what is meant, often with a mocking edge.

clue.text: In the past dry, yet sea rough …

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Weather report: earlier it was dry, but the sea was choppy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning on the day before today, or more loosely in former times, fits 'in the past'.

clue.text: Prehistoric flint head of the Spanish distant conflict

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
distant means far
a row is a quarrel or conflict

explanation.surface: An ancient arrowhead from a long-ago war in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Elf-arrow is the folk name for a Neolithic flint arrowhead, once thought to be shot by fairies.

clue.text: … soon, for example, about half London may be engulfed

indicators.note: the pieces are swallowed up inside the abbreviation for an example

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: half of the six-letter city name gives its first three letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: soon perhaps half of London will be swamped.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the surface on from the clue before; 'may be engulfed' is the container signal, with the about-and-half-London pieces swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere long is an old-fashioned way of saying before much time passes, i.e. shortly.

clue.text: Chuck, for starters, fish left in neighbour's garage

indicators.note: for starters points to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A fish is dumped in the garage next door.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw or hurl something, the same as to chuck it.

clue.text: Quick answer in practice is incentive to get up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a rite is a customary ritual practice

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means reading the word from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a sop is something given to placate or induce, an incentive

explanation.surface: In training, a reward motivates rising early.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to get up' reads the incentive upwards, giving POS; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, originally a fencer's swift return thrust.

clue.text: Almost never related to astronomy!

parts.note: a phrase for something very rare that literally refers to a lunar event

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very rarely, and literally names a second full moon in a month, an astronomical event.

clue.text: Use ropes flexibly on the surface, raised in relief

definitions.text: on the surface, raised in relief

indicators.note: flexibly suggests the letters are bent into another arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction for using ropes with suppleness on some surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Repousse metalwork is hammered from behind so the design stands raised on the front face.

clue.text: How did little devil behave? With shock!

parts.note: an imp is a small devil or mischievous child
to act is to behave in a certain way

explanation.surface: A question about a naughty child's conduct, with the shocked answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the force of a collision, a jolt or shock.

clue.text: Sheriff yodelling is a bit dubious

indicators.note: the answer is just a bit, a small stretch, of the following words

explanation.surface: A lawman's yodelling is somewhat questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or of uncertain quality.

clue.text: So a hug upset outstanding girl? 15 needed!

indicators.note: read as standing out, i.e. outside, the girl's name wraps the other letters

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked into another order

explanation.surface: An excellent girl is upset by a hug, and no remark is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes OUGHSA from SO A HUG, and 'outstanding' places ENID outside it. 15 is the answer to 15-down, a phrase refusing to say more.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom declares that nothing more need be said, much as refusing to remark on something does.

clue.text: Regenerates us? Does getting pickled?

indicators.note: regenerating remakes something, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Questions about whether pickling revives a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused means steeped in brine or vinegar, and also drunk; both match pickled.

clue.text: Charlie gets back around mid-morning, overdue — turning a dull grey colour

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the single middle letter
gets back means the word for a fool is read backwards

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is a mug
the middle letter of the word morning

indicators.note: turning means the word for overdue is read backwards

parts.note: overdue means late

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie returns late in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets back' reverses the fool, giving GUM; 'turning' reverses overdue, giving ETAL. Charlie is slang for a fool, not a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmetal is a dark bluish-grey shade named after the bronze alloy once used for guns.

clue.text: On about messieurs (in French) getting into bed — my lips are sealed

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the abbreviation and French word get inside the little bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MM is the abbreviation for messieurs
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Frenchmen climb into bed while someone refuses to say a word about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses On, giving NO. The parenthesis makes 'in French' look like an aside, but it supplies EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying my lips are sealed is a refusal to say anything, a standard reply to the press.

clue.text: Stone me! Belonged to you a long time ago, in a way

indicators.note: in sets the pronouns inside the article plus street

parts.note: a, plus ST, street, a way
taken as written

parts.words: Belonged to you a long time ago
parts.note: thy is the archaic word for your, belonging to you

explanation.surface: Stone me! An exclamation about something that was once yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' looks like an oath; only 'Stone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Harder time getting old? How repugnant for the Queen

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Ageing gets harder, and the Queen finds it disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tougher is the comparative of tough, meaning more difficult or firmer.

clue.text: Protective cover, enough for a very little tot

definitions.meaning: a cap worn on a fingertip to guard it when sewing

definitions.text: enough for a very little tot
definitions.meaning: a thimbleful is a tiny measure of drink, a tot

explanation.definitionFit: A thimble shields the finger in sewing, and as a measure means just a drop of liquor.

clue.text: Fetching a number of Romans by order to see

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
OM is the Order of Merit
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Romans arranged in order go to a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely means attractive, and fetching is a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Home counties copper, god of the house, is beginning to move to a worldly way of thinking

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a lar is a Roman household god
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A policeman from near London, who worships a household deity, starts turning to materialism.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Secularism is the outlook that excludes religion, concerned with worldly rather than spiritual matters.

clue.text: A key that leads to a hitch?

parts.note: a key, or cay, is a low island, an isle

explanation.surface: A question about some key that might cause a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' means getting hitched, married: one walks up this to the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's central passage is what a bride walks along to get married.

clue.text: Quits flat

definitions.meaning: being quits means owing nothing, all square

explanation.definitionFit: Even means both squared up after a debt and level or smooth in surface.

clue.text: English bishop takes gold? Whoops!

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An English bishop pockets gold, and oops.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoops is the cry uttered on making a blunder, so it stands for the mistake itself.

clue.text: Crooked cashier withdrawing a lot of material possessions

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A dishonest bank teller takes out a great deal of property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' takes the A out of CASHIER; the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches means wealth, a great store of money and goods.

clue.text: Overcome journey, say, from the kitchen garden?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: to overcome is to beat; a route is the way of a journey

explanation.surface: Has a tiring trip been beaten, perhaps by something from the vegetable patch?
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a root vegetable commonly grown in a kitchen garden, an example of its produce.

clue.text: Distress with endless problems one day before

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: aggro is British slang for trouble or problems
I is the Roman numeral one
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: Trouble keeps coming, upsetting someone on the eve of something.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO is British slang for aggravation or trouble; 'endless' leaves AGGR.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause someone distress or a sense of injustice.

clue.text: Cast, say, from Windsor chair?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: cast means thrown

explanation.surface: A chair hurled out of Windsor, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A Windsor chair is a furniture style, but here it means the seat of the House of Windsor, the British royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal seat of the Windsor monarchs is their throne, a ceremonial chair.
